negative_reviews.author: Breanna Hill
negative_reviews.text: I got food poisoning from the chicken ramen, had me throwing up all night and overall the atmosphere didn’t feel that clean, there’s no ventilation. wouldn’t recommend.

negative_reviews.author: V V
negative_reviews.text:
The Asian girl with black  pony tail that works there is super rude!!
Went in to have ramen today and they had some sort of voucher in their app for £5 ramen they even had some leaflets with their apps QR code on the table so I asked the server girl how it works, she immediately lied saying the app takes an hour to load the offer when it only took me 15mins and after I told her I already have my voucher from the app and didn’t take an hour she roller her eyes and got so irritated. If you don’t want customers to use the voucher from your app why would you even advertise it?!

negative_reviews.author: Alex Bell
negative_reviews.text: Food was 50/50, portions were small, egg white was raw, noodles were undercooked, rolls fall apart. Nice atmosphere

negative_reviews.author: Johura Islam
negative_reviews.text: The service was alright but it was too expensive. The ramen was too salty and the noodles were not cooked enough. I also found hair on my tap water.

deliveroo.source: Deliveroo Weekly Dash PDF overview (Sales Overview) — gap-site weekly sales; ops metrics not in this source. + ops from Weekly Summary sheet

issues: Covers rose by 119 (6.74%) to 1,884 week on week, while spend per head fell by £1.70 (8.16%) to £19.14 (the report shows the SPH change as +£1.70).
The site links more covers and lower SPH to the loyalty app and discount platforms such as First Table, Fork, CodeApp and TasteCard.
Sales were £38,303.31, up £40.27 (0.10%) week on week and £2,803.30 (7.90%) above the £35,500 target.
Kobas figures show £5,274.87 of discounts and £3,928.87 of staff food, giving adjusted sales of £42,232.17 and labour of 24.3% (FOH 12.50%, 11.31% after discount; BOH 14.55%, 13.20% after discount).
In the meeting, wage cost was 26.88% excluding discounts (below 25% including discounts) and food cost was 27.79%.
Delivery sales were about £1.8K, and Ziang Lin sees delivery as the main way to grow sales and offset labour, targeting £4K to £5K a week.
A 20% to 30% delivery discount runs on Thursday and Sunday this week, followed by an all day Monday to Thursday delivery promotion from next week.

The delivery packing station needs streamlining to stop missing items during rushes, and delivery bags must carry Post-it notes, A6 app QR flyers, £5 vouchers and, for Slurp, loyalty and reorder cards.
A 50% off Slurp promotion is coming, so staff should prepare for much higher order volumes.
All Deliveroo reviews were answered and there were no refund claims.
Google rating stands at 4.7, with 65 five star, 2 four star, 2 three star, no two star and 2 one star reviews this week (the meeting quoted 4.74 and 62 five star).
One guest changed a 1 star review to 5 stars after service recovery, and another 1 star review has been addressed.
The BOH meeting noted a 1 star review alleging food poisoning from the chicken ramen and unclean ventilation, on top of earlier feedback about salty ramen, undercooked noodles and high prices.

Noodles were reported as hard and undercooked, so staff must boil the water fully and cook noodles for one minute twenty seconds, and FOH management now carries out food quality checks five times a day.

The site ran out of noodles, chicken broth and beef despite normal food cost percentages; the head chef cited heavy ordering and possible delivery discrepancies, and actual spend was transcribed as 10,644.3.
The kitchen is concerned the food budget is too small, fish is bought daily, and staff food figures also include Nori.
Wait times of 40 minutes on sushi tickets were flagged as a floor management issue.
Kitchen labour needs to be saved methodically while giving the kitchen team longer breaks, and invoice management and communication from the kitchen need to improve.
There is a leaking pipe near the drainage, Ross is sending someone to fix the drainage, and the extractors have been cleaned; all maintenance is logged.
Ian will coordinate a full site revamp covering upstairs, downstairs and the bathrooms.
The sushi bar and bar were deep cleaned, and waste is being recorded on Kobas for FOH and bar, with BOH to monitor food cost and waste more closely.
A new KP and a new kitchen assistant have been hired, two hires (a full time KP and a chef starting the next day) are replacing a leaver, and a former team member, Tamara, might return.
Imi is on holiday, and Caitlyn will work three days a week at Soho to cut shifts and labour while Ziang Lin is on holiday.
The report asks which compliance tracker London sites should use (the SE/Midlands tracker).
Upcoming promotions are Halloween, Fork loyalty, First Table, a special lunch, Tastecard and CodeApp.
Areas for improvement are kitchen food quality, keeping up cleaning standards, FOH and BOH communication during shifts, and setting a stable standard for operations and service.
Sunspel on Old Compton Street was set up for the 15% B2B staff discount.
